knowledge_abstraction.general_principle: Indexing operations may assume non-empty slice outputs and can produce incorrect shapes or values when a slice range is empty, especially when combined with non-empty slices or downstream shape-dependent operations.

risk_dimensions.shape: Zero-length slice ranges where start equals stop, empty dimensions mixed with non-empty dimensions, and subsequent indexing or reshaping of empty results.
risk_dimensions.dtype: Integer index dtypes and output dtype preservation on empty tensors may be underexplored.
risk_dimensions.memory: Contiguous versus view-based tensors and zero-numel storage layouts may expose hidden assumptions.
risk_dimensions.device: CPU and CUDA backends may diverge in empty slice handling.
risk_dimensions.execution_state: Operations after empty slicing such as reshape, reduction, or further indexing may carry invalid state assumptions.

failure_mechanism.description: Shape inference or dispatch for indexing may not correctly propagate zero-length slice dimensions, causing downstream operators to receive inconsistent shape metadata or compute wrong results.

input_exploration: Explore slice bounds producing start equals stop and empty ranges across one or more axes
Combine empty slices with non-empty slices and with zero-sized input dimensions
Apply follow-up operations such as further indexing, reshaping, and reductions to empty slice results
Test both contiguous and view-based tensors, including zero-numel tensors
constraint_awareness: Empty slice outputs must have zero extent in the corresponding dimension
Downstream shape-dependent operations must not assume at least one element
Result dtype and shape should match explicitly constructed empty tensors
oracle_strategy: Compare output shape, dtype, and values to explicit empty tensor construction
Monitor for incorrect values, shape mismatches, or crashes in subsequent operations
Use standard tensor library semantics as reference for empty slicing behavior

transferability.reason: Zero-length dimension handling is a general shape boundary concern across slicing, indexing, and shape-dependent operators, but the exact failure conditions depend on each API's shape inference and dispatch implementation.

important_considerations: Probe shape boundaries where one dimension becomes zero while other dimensions remain non-empty
Exercise downstream shape-changing operations on empty slice results
Include both view and contiguous tensor inputs to expose memory layout assumptions
generation_strategy: Generate harnesses that vary slice bounds to produce empty dimensions, compare results against explicit empty tensor semantics, and apply follow-up shape-dependent operations to detect incorrect propagation of empty shapes.
